ENGLISH LANGUAGE — MOCK EXAM #8
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. A minimal pair is two words that (1 mark)
   A. differ in only one sound
   B. rhyme with each other
   C. have the same spelling
   D. mean the same thing

2. Which word begins with the blend tw? (1 mark)
   A. tenth
   B. tender
   C. twenty
   D. tennis

3. 'I saw a goat. ___ goat was brown.' Which article fits the blank? (1 mark)
   A. A
   B. An
   C. Some
   D. The

4. What does 'DOB' mean on a form? (1 mark)
   A. Date of birth
   B. Date of book
   C. Day of business
   D. Duty of boy

5. 'Sleep like a log' means (1 mark)
   A. sleep very little
   B. sleep very deeply
   C. wake up early
   D. sleep in the forest

6. Which part of a composition tells who, where and when? (1 mark)
   A. The introduction
   B. The conclusion
   C. The body
   D. The title only

7. Which phrase do we use to get someone's attention politely? (1 mark)
   A. Give me
   B. Hey you
   C. Move away
   D. Excuse me

8. Which of these words is written with a double consonant in the middle? (1 mark)
   A. stop
   B. play
   C. dinner
   D. drink

9. First aid words: Which word has the sound /aɪ/? (1 mark)
   A. stop
   B. box
   C. hot
   D. bite

10. A friendly letter is written to (1 mark)
   A. someone you know well
   B. the government only
   C. a stranger only
   D. nobody

11. Which quantifier goes with a countable plural noun in a question? (1 mark)
   A. a little
   B. less
   C. many
   D. much

12. In a picture series, which picture usually shows the ending? (1 mark)
   A. The middle picture
   B. The last picture
   C. None of them
   D. The first picture

13. A good title for a story about a boy who emails his grandmother is (1 mark)
   A. A Trip to the Farm
   B. The Weather in April
   C. How to Bake Bread
   D. A Message for Grandmother

14. What is turn-taking in a conversation? (1 mark)
   A. One person speaks all the time
   B. One person speaks while the other listens, then they swap
   C. Both people speak at the same time
   D. Only the teacher speaks

15. Which helping verb completes: 'They ____ watching TV when the power went off.'? (1 mark)
   A. were
   B. was
   C. am
   D. is

16. How is the sound /v/ made? (1 mark)
   A. The mouth is closed and air passes through the nose
   B. The tongue touches the roof and there is no voice
   C. The lips are rounded and do not touch the teeth
   D. The upper teeth touch the lower lip and the voice buzzes

17. What is a shed on a farm? (1 mark)
   A. A person who works on a farm
   B. A small building for tools or animals
   C. A tool for digging
   D. A kind of crop

18. Which word helps to show the order of events? (1 mark)
   A. green
   B. heavy
   C. farm
   D. suddenly

19. Which word begins with /z/? (1 mark)
   A. sit
   B. sad
   C. zebra
   D. sun

20. In which word does the letter s say /z/? (1 mark)
   A. easy
   B. sit
   C. sun
   D. class

21. Which is an adverb of time meaning 'not at any time'? (1 mark)
   A. usually
   B. never
   C. sometimes
   D. often

22. Which sentence should end with a full stop, not a question mark? (1 mark)
   A. Are you ready
   B. She asked where the clinic was.
   C. What is her name
   D. Where is the clinic

23. Which sentence asks about time and needs a question mark at the end? (1 mark)
   A. Please sit down
   B. We won the match
   C. When does the match start
   D. The match starts at ten

24. Which is the correct spelling? (1 mark)
   A. necessery
   B. necesary
   C. neccessary
   D. necessary

25. Which is a yes/no question? (1 mark)
   A. Where is the bin?
   B. What did you sweep?
   C. Is the compound clean?
   D. Who is the captain?

26. What must a diary entry begin with? (1 mark)
   A. A question
   B. A friend's name
   C. A title in capitals
   D. The day and date

27. Which sentence uses the pattern 'very ... but ...' correctly? (1 mark)
   A. The shirt very nice but expensive.
   B. The shirt is very nice, but it is too expensive.
   C. Very shirt is nice, but.
   D. The shirt is but very nice, it is expensive.

28. What does 'scanning' mean? (1 mark)
   A. Reading every word slowly
   B. Drawing a picture
   C. Looking quickly for one detail such as a name or number
   D. Copying the text

29. Which word has a double consonant? (1 mark)
   A. later
   B. letter
   C. river
   D. paper

30. Which word means 'jumping on one leg'? (1 mark)
   A. hoping
   B. hopping
   C. hopeing
   D. hopped

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Write three sentences using three of these words: because, different, address, favourite, tomorrow. (3 marks)

32. State the difference between a factual question and an inferential question. (2 marks)

33. Name the three parts of fluent reading and explain each briefly. (3 marks)

34. Punctuate: 'we planted maize beans and sorghum' (2 marks)

35. Give three words with silent letters and name the silent letter in each. (3 marks)

36. Fill in the double letters: di__er, ye__ow, bu__on. (3 marks)

37. Explain how to use the five-finger test. (3 marks)

38. Write the comparative and superlative of: happy, beautiful. (2 marks)

39. Describe the steps to interpret a picture. (3 marks)

40. Arrange in alphabetical order: goat, cow, hen, dog. (2 marks)

41. Write a short dialogue of four lines in which you borrow a book from a friend politely. (4 marks)

42. Write a short speech of four sentences about protecting a river. (4 marks)

43. Explain the rule for changing nouns that end in y into plurals. Give two examples. (3 marks)

44. Mark the words you would stress in: 'We must keep our compound clean.' (3 marks)

45. Explain the difference between a fact and an opinion. Give one example of each. (3 marks)

46. List three hygiene habits mentioned in the text. (3 marks)

47. Write two words in which 'gh' is silent and two in which it says /f/. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — MOCK EXAM #8 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — differ in only one sound
   For example tin and din differ only in the first sound.

2. C — twenty
   Twenty starts with t and w together.

3. D — The
   The goat has already been mentioned, so we use the.

4. A — Date of birth
   DOB is short for date of birth.

5. B — sleep very deeply
   A log does not move, so it means a deep sleep.

6. A — The introduction
   The introduction sets the scene.

7. D — Excuse me
   Excuse me is polite.

8. C — dinner
   Dinner has double n.

9. D — bite
   Bite has /aɪ/.

10. A — someone you know well
   A friendly letter is personal.

11. C — many
   How many books?

12. B — The last picture
   The last picture usually shows how it finished.

13. D — A Message for Grandmother
   It suits the story.

14. B — One person speaks while the other listens, then they swap
   In turn-taking each speaker waits for the other to finish before speaking.

15. A — were
   'They' takes 'were' in the past progressive.

16. D — The upper teeth touch the lower lip and the voice buzzes
   /v/ uses teeth and lip; /w/ uses rounded lips only.

17. B — A small building for tools or animals
   A shed is used for storing tools or sheltering animals.

18. D — suddenly
   'Suddenly' is a time word.

19. C — zebra
   'Zebra' begins with the buzzing /z/.

20. A — easy
   The s in 'easy' is buzzed, like z.

21. B — never
   'Never' means at no time.

22. B — She asked where the clinic was.
   It reports a question, so it is a statement.

23. C — When does the match start
   It is a direct question.

24. D — necessary
   One c and two s's.

25. C — Is the compound clean?
   It starts with a helping verb and can be answered yes or no.

26. D — The day and date
   Every entry is dated.

27. B — The shirt is very nice, but it is too expensive.
   It has 'very' + adjective, then 'but' with the difficulty.

28. C — Looking quickly for one detail such as a name or number
   Scanning searches for specific information.

29. B — letter
   'Letter' has a double t.

30. B — hopping
   Hopping has a double p; hoping means wishing.

SECTION B
----
31. (3 marks)
   Answer: Any three correct sentences using the words with correct spelling.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

32. (2 marks)
   Answer: A factual question has an answer stated in the text. An inferential question needs you to use clues and think.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each type.

33. (3 marks)
   Answer: Accuracy: reading the words correctly. Speed: reading at a comfortable, not rushed pace. Expression: using the voice to show meaning and feeling.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part explained.

34. (2 marks)
   Answer: We planted maize, beans and sorghum.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each comma and capital/full stop.

35. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example: knee (k), debt (b), honest (h).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each word with its silent letter.

36. (3 marks)
   Answer: dinner, yellow, button
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

37. (3 marks)
   Answer: Open a page and read. Hold up a finger for each new word. Count the fingers: few means the book is right, many means it is too hard.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the method, 1 mark for few, 1 mark for many.

38. (2 marks)
   Answer: happier, happiest; more beautiful, most beautiful.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

39. (3 marks)
   Answer: Look at the whole picture, read the caption, notice details and expressions, think what is happening and what will happen next.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of three steps.

40. (2 marks)
   Answer: cow, dog, goat, hen
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for c and d first, 1 mark for g and h last.

41. (4 marks)
   Answer: A: Good morning, Ali. B: Good morning. A: May I borrow your book, please? B: Yes, here you are. A: Thank you.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for greeting, request, answer and thanks.

42. (4 marks)
   Answer: A greeting, two points such as not throwing rubbish in the river and planting trees on its bank, and a closing.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each element.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: If a consonant comes before y, change y to i and add es (baby, babies). If a vowel comes before y, add s (boy, boys).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule and 1 mark for correct examples.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: We must KEEP our COMpound CLEAN. (Important words: keep, compound, clean.)
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each important word.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: A fact can be checked, for example 'Germs are tiny'. An opinion says what someone thinks, for example 'Cold water is nicest'.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each definition and 1 for examples.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: Wash hands with soap; boil drinking water; use a clean latrine; cover food; brush teeth; cut nails short.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

47. (4 marks)
   Answer: Silent: night, light, high, daughter (any two). /f/: laugh, cough, enough, rough (any two).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct word.
